page: Amazon Web Services r4.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It is driven by Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processors with an x86_64 architecture, providing 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 488.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB per vCPU, and is supported by a 45 MB L3 cache. It lacks integrated local instance storage and includes no discrete graphics processing hardware, relying on network-attached storage and standard compute pipelines, while providing a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a significant split between per-thread throughput and aggregate parallel capacity. Single-core evaluations reflect legacy performance tiers, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 909.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 868.89, both ranking in the bottom 10%. However, across all 64 vCPUs, parallel compute metrics achieve average tier results, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8878.0, a PassMark CPU score of 32455.54, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 29203.03. Memory read bandwidth reaches 106.11 GB/sec on large 256MB blocks, with Redis SET operations sustaining 35.7 million operations per second.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency perspective, the r4.16xlarge prioritizes substantial memory density and multi-core parallel scaling over per-core instruction efficiency. The absence of modern instruction extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX limits throughput for intensive mathematical transformations and larger machine learning pipelines, where 7B parameter LLM text generation is restricted to 8.05 tokens per second. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-bound, distributed enterprise workloads such as large in-memory databases, caching tiers, batch processing, and memory-heavy ETL pipelines that do not depend on high single-threaded clock frequencies.
description: Amazon Web Services r4.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Equipped with 488.0 GB of RAM (7.62 GB per vCPU), a 45 MB L3 cache, and 25 Gbps baseline network throughput, this instance is tailored for workloads requiring massive memory footprints. It does not include local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark data indicates modest single-core throughput, placing in the lower percentiles across Geekbench and stress-ng tests, but delivers steady mid-tier performance across multi-threaded evaluations, including a PassMark CPU score of 32455.54 and 35.7 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking AVX-512 extensions, it is less efficient for advanced numerical computing or intensive AI generation. The r4.16xlarge is strategically suited for large-scale caching clusters, in-memory databases, batch data transformations, and general enterprise memory-intensive applications.
